newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourse closes up, helped by dollar.
newsitem.headline: German bourse closes up, helped by dollar.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade slightly firmer on Thursday having been hoisted by a slightly firmer dollar which managed to lessen the impact of Wednesday's sharp decline on Wall Street.
The 30-share blue chip DAX index closed bourse trading up 6.03 points higher at 2,847.08 having come off its session high at 2,852.44.
This afternoon the market will keep its eye on Wall Street for more trading direction.

Dealers said the firmer dollar, trading at 1.5440 marks, was largely responsible for boosting the market today after it closely mirrored Wall Street's movements, falling in after-hours trading on Wednesday but recovering this morning.
The firmer dollar is particularly helpful for export sensitive shares, including chemicals.

Among the chemicals sector, Hoechst AG, fresh from announcing it would sell its specialty chemicals business to Swiss group Clariant AG and would buy the remaining stake in French drugs group Roussel-Uclaf, is still generating interest.
The shares closed up 2.43 marks at 73.28, just below a record high of 73.40.
Separately electronics and engineering giant Siemens AG closed down 65 pfennigs 72.55 marks down after a slew of mixed news, which some dealers thought was positive, although others disagreed.

Shipmaker Bremer Vulkan, once Germany's biggest shipyard, was the session's biggest loser closing down 35 pfennigs at two marks, as the bankrupt company said on Wednesday it had only enough money to keep its flagship yard open through the end of this year.
